h: Wild coast and a famous invasion
p: The coastline around Goodwick is some of the most dramatic in Wales, and a short drive west brings you to Strumble Head, where a lighthouse sits on a small island just off the cliffs. It's a favourite spot for watching the sea, and patient visitors are often rewarded with sightings of porpoises, dolphins, seals and seabirds. The old wartime lookout on the headland makes a handy shelter on blustery days.

This corner of Pembrokeshire also has a remarkable claim to fame. In 1797, French troops landed at Carregwastad Point near Goodwick, in what is often called the last invasion of mainland Britain. The invasion was quickly defeated, and the story is told in the Last Invasion Tapestry, a huge embroidered artwork on display in Fishguard. It's a fascinating piece of local history and well worth seeing.
Lower Fishguard, with its pretty harbour and cottages, was used as a filming location for Under Milk Wood in the early 1970s, starring Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor.
If you're keen to spot wildlife at sea, bring binoculars, check the weather and be patient. Calm days with little wind are best, as fins and splashes are much easier to spot.
Combine your visit with a stretch of the Pembrokeshire Coast Path for a proper day out on the wild Welsh coast. It's a quieter, wilder slice of Wales, and all the better for it.
